title_en: Civil Servant Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated in accordance with the Constitution with a view to regulating the administration of public servants, safeguarding their lawful rights and interests, strengthening supervision over them, promoting their proper performance of duties and responsibilities, and building a contingent of high-quality and professional public servants who are firm in conviction, dedicated to serving the people, diligent and pragmatic, courageous in taking responsibility, and upright and honest.

Article 2 For the purposes of this Law, "public servants" means staff members who perform public duties according to law, are included in the state administrative staffing, and whose salaries and benefits are borne by the state finance.
Public servants are an important part of the cadre contingent, the backbone of the socialist cause, and the public servants of the people.

Article 3 The obligations, rights, and administration of public servants shall be governed by this Law.
Where laws provide otherwise for the selection, appointment and removal, supervision of leading members among public servants, as well as the obligations, rights, and administration of supervisory officials, judges, prosecutors, etc., those provisions shall prevail.

Article 4 The system of public servants shall adhere to the leadership of the Communist Party of China, be guided by Marxism-Leninism, Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the important thought of Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, implement the basic line of the primary stage of socialism, implement the organizational line of the Communist Party of China in the new era, and adhere to the principle of the Party assuming the responsibility for cadre management.

Article 5 The administration of public servants shall adhere to the principles of openness, equality, competition, and selection of the best, and shall be conducted in accordance with the statutory authority, conditions, standards, and procedures.
Article 6 The administration of public servants shall adhere to the principle of giving equal importance to supervision and restraint as well as incentives and guarantees.

Article 7 The appointment of public servants shall adhere to the principles of both integrity and ability, with priority given to integrity; of recruiting from all over the country and appointing people on their merits; and of giving priority to the cause and being fair and upright, with emphasis on political criteria and attention to actual work performance.
Article 8 The state shall implement classified administration of public servants to improve management efficiency and scientific level.
Article 9 When assuming office, a public servant shall take a public oath of allegiance to the Constitution in accordance with legal provisions.
Article 10 The acts of a public servant in performing duties according to law shall be protected by law.
Article 11 The funds required for the salaries, benefits, insurance, recruitment, rewards, training, dismissal, etc. of public servants shall be included in the fiscal budget and guaranteed.

Article 12 The central competent department of public servants shall be responsible for the comprehensive administration of public servants nationwide. The competent departments of public servants at or above the county level in local areas shall be responsible for the comprehensive administration of public servants within their respective jurisdictions. The competent department of public servants at a higher level shall guide the administration of public servants by the competent department of public servants at a lower level. The competent departments of public servants at each level shall guide the administration of public servants by the various organs at the same level.

Article 16 The state shall implement a position classification system for public servants.
The categories of public servant positions shall be divided into categories such as comprehensive management, professional technology, and administrative enforcement according to the nature, characteristics, and management needs of the positions. In accordance with this Law, other position categories may be added for positions with particularities requiring separate management. The scope of application of each position category shall be separately prescribed by the state.

Article 17 The state shall implement a system where the positions and ranks of public servants run in parallel, and shall set up the sequences of leading positions and ranks of public servants according to the categories and duties of public servant positions.

Article 18 The leading positions of public servants shall be established in accordance with the Constitution, relevant laws, and organizational specifications.
The levels of leading positions are divided into: national-level principal, national-level deputy; provincial/ministerial-level principal, provincial/ministerial-level deputy; bureau/department-level principal, bureau/department-level deputy; county/section-level principal, county/section-level deputy; township/section-level principal, township/section-level deputy.

Article 19 The ranks of public servants shall be established at or below the bureau/department level.
The sequence of ranks for public servants in the comprehensive management category is divided into: Level 1 Inspector, Level 2 Inspector, Level 1 Researcher, Level 2 Researcher, Level 3 Researcher, Level 4 Researcher, Level 1 Principal Staff Member, Level 2 Principal Staff Member, Level 3 Principal Staff Member, Level 4 Principal Staff Member, Level 1 Staff Member, Level 2 Staff Member.
The rank sequences for public servants in position categories other than the comprehensive management category shall be separately prescribed by the state in accordance with this Law.

Article 20 Each organ shall, in accordance with the established functions, specifications, staffing limits, number of positions, and structural proportions, set up specific public servant positions within the organ and determine the job responsibilities and qualification requirements for each position.

Article 21 The leading positions and ranks of public servants shall correspond to appropriate grades. The corresponding relationship between leading positions, ranks, and grades of public servants shall be prescribed by the State.
According to work needs and the corresponding relationship between leading positions and ranks, the leading positions and ranks held by public servants may be mutually transferred or concurrently held; if the qualifications prescribed by provisions are met, they may be promoted to leading positions or ranks.
The grade of a public servant shall be determined based on the leading position, rank, and his or her moral integrity, capability, work performance, and seniority. A public servant at the same leading position or rank may be promoted in grade in accordance with the provisions of the State.
The leading position, rank, and grade of a public servant shall be the basis for determining the salary and other treatment of the public servant.

Article 22 The State shall, based on the work characteristics of public servants such as the people's police, fire and rescue personnel, customs officers, and diplomatic missions stationed abroad, establish ranks corresponding to their leading positions and ranks.

Article 23 The recruitment of public servants holding positions at or below the level of Principal Staff Member, Grade 1, and other equivalent rank levels shall adopt the methods of open examinations, strict assessment, equal competition, and择优录取 (selection based on merit).
When recruiting public servants in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph in ethnic autonomous areas, appropriate preferential treatment shall be given to candidates from ethnic minorities in accordance with laws and relevant provisions.

Article 24 The recruitment of public servants by central organs and their subsidiary units shall be organized by the central public servant competent department. The recruitment of public servants by local organs at various levels shall be organized by the provincial public servant competent department; when necessary, the provincial public servant competent department may authorize the public servant competent department of a city divided into districts to organize the recruitment.

Article 25 To apply for a position as a public servant, in addition to meeting the conditions prescribed in Article 13 of this Law, an applicant shall also meet the qualifications required for the proposed position as prescribed by the provincial or higher level public servant competent department.
The State shall implement a unified legal professional qualification examination system for public servants who are initially engaged in the review of administrative penalty decisions, administrative reconsideration, administrative adjudication, and legal advisory work in administrative organs, which shall be organized and implemented by the judicial administrative department of the State Council in consultation with relevant departments.
Article 27 The recruitment of public servants shall be conducted within the prescribed staffing limits and with corresponding vacant positions.

Article 28 For the recruitment of public servants, a recruitment announcement shall be issued. The recruitment announcement shall specify the positions to be recruited, the number of positions, the qualification requirements for applicants, the application materials required for application, and other matters that applicants need to know.
The recruiting organ shall take measures to facilitate citizens' application.

Article 29 The recruiting organ shall examine the applications based on the qualification requirements for applicants. The application materials submitted by applicants shall be truthful and accurate.

Article 30 The recruitment examination for public servants shall be conducted by means of written examinations, interviews, etc., and the content of the examinations shall be set separately according to the basic capabilities that public servants shall possess and the different categories of positions and different levels of organs.

Article 31 The recruiting organ shall determine the candidates for investigation based on the examination results, and conduct a review of application qualifications, investigation, and physical examination.
The items and standards of physical examination shall be determined according to the requirements of the position. The specific measures shall be prescribed by the central public servant competent department jointly with the health administrative department of the State Council.

Article 32 The recruiting organ shall, based on the examination results, investigation situation, and physical examination results, propose a list of candidates to be recruited and make it public. The publicity period shall not be less than five working days.
Upon expiration of the publicity period, the central level recruiting organ shall report the list of candidates to be recruited to the central public servant competent department for filing; local recruiting organs at various levels shall report the list of candidates to be recruited to the provincial or municipal (city divided into districts) public servant competent department for approval.

Article 33 For the recruitment of public servants for special positions, with the approval of the provincial or higher level public servant competent department, simplified procedures or other assessment methods may be adopted.
Article 34 The probation period for newly recruited public servants shall be one year. Those who pass the probation period shall be appointed; those who fail shall have their recruitment canceled.

Article 35 The assessment of public servants shall, in accordance with the management authority, comprehensively assess the public servant's virtue, capability, diligence, performance, and integrity, with emphasis on political quality and work performance. The assessment indicators shall be set separately according to different categories of positions and different levels of organs.

Article 36 The assessment of public servants shall be divided into methods such as daily assessment, special assessment, and regular assessment. Regular assessment shall be based on daily assessment and special assessment.

Article 37 The regular assessment of public servants who are not leading members shall adopt the method of annual assessment. First, the individual shall make a summary according to the duties of the position and relevant requirements; after listening to the opinions of the masses, the supervisory leader shall propose a recommendation for the assessment grade, and the person in charge of the organ or the authorized assessment committee shall determine the assessment grade.
The assessment of leading members shall be handled by the supervisory organ in accordance with relevant provisions.

Article 38 The results of regular assessment shall be divided into four grades: excellent, competent, basically competent, and incompetent.
The results of regular assessment shall be notified to the public servant in writing.

Article 39 The results of regular assessment shall serve as the basis for adjusting the position, leading position, rank, grade, salary of the public servant, as well as for rewards, training, and dismissal of public servants.

Article 40 The leading positions of public servants shall adopt the systems of election, appointment, and employment. The ranks of public servants shall adopt the systems of appointment and employment.
The positions of leading members shall adopt the term system in accordance with the provisions of the State.

Article 41 A civil servant selected through election shall assume the elected position when the election result takes effect; if the term of office expires and no reappointment occurs, or if resignation, removal, or dismissal happens during the term, the position held shall terminate.

Article 42 For a civil servant appointed by appointment, if the probation period expires and the assessment is passed, or if the position or rank changes, or in other circumstances where appointment or removal of a position or rank is necessary, the appointment or removal shall be carried out in accordance with the administrative authority and the prescribed procedures.
Article 43 The appointment of a civil servant shall be made within the prescribed authorized size and number of positions, and there shall be corresponding vacancies.

Article 44 A civil servant who needs to hold a part-time position outside the organ due to work requirements shall obtain approval from the relevant organ and shall not receive any remuneration for such part-time position.

Article 45 A civil servant who is promoted to a leading position shall possess the conditions and qualifications required for the proposed position in terms of political quality, work ability, educational level, and service experience.
The leading positions of civil servants shall be promoted level by level. Those who are particularly outstanding or have special work needs may be promoted by skipping levels or breaking the routine in accordance with the provisions.

Article 47 If a leading position at or below the principal level of department or bureau level becomes vacant and there is no suitable candidate within the organ, the candidate for the position may be selected from society through appropriate means.

Article 48 A civil servant who is promoted to a leading position shall be subject to a pre-appointment public notice system and a probationary period system for the position in accordance with the relevant provisions.

Article 49 The rank of a civil servant shall be promoted level by level. The candidate shall be determined based on the individual's moral and professional performance, actual work achievements, and service seniority, with reference to the results of democratic recommendation or democratic evaluation. After public notice, the promotion shall be approved in accordance with the administrative authority.

Article 50 The positions and ranks of civil servants shall be subject to a system of both promotion and demotion. Those who are unsuitable or incompetent for their current positions or ranks shall be adjusted.
If a civil servant is determined to be incompetent in the annual assessment, his or her position or rank shall be reduced by one level in accordance with the prescribed procedures.

Article 51 Awards shall be given to civil servants or civil servant collectives that have outstanding work performance, remarkable achievements and contributions, or other outstanding deeds. Awards shall adhere to the principle of combining regular awards with timely awards, and combining spiritual awards with material awards, with spiritual awards as the main focus.
Awards for civil servant collectives shall apply to organs established in accordance with the authorized establishment sequence or working groups formed to complete special tasks.

Article 53 Awards are classified as: commendation, recording of third-class merit, recording of second-class merit, recording of first-class merit, and conferring of titles.
The awarded civil servant or civil servant collective shall be cited, and the awarded individual shall be given a one-time monetary bonus or other benefits.
Article 54 The decision or approval of giving an award to a civil servant or a civil servant collective shall be made in accordance with the prescribed authority and procedures.
Article 55 In accordance with state provisions, commemorative certificates or badges may be issued to civil servants who have participated in major work in specific periods or specific fields.

Article 57 The organ shall supervise the civil servant's ideological and political status, performance of duties, work style, and compliance with laws and disciplines, carry out education on diligence and integrity, and establish a daily management and supervision system.
If problems are discovered through supervision of civil servants, depending on the circumstances, the organ shall provide conversation reminders, criticism and education, ordered inspection, admonition, organizational adjustment, or sanctions.
If a civil servant is suspected of duty-related violations or crimes, the matter shall be transferred to the supervisory authority for handling according to law.
Article 58 A civil servant shall consciously accept supervision, and shall request instructions and report on work, and report personal matters as required.

Article 60 When a civil servant is performing official duties and believes that a decision or order of a superior is erroneous, the civil servant may propose to the superior an opinion to correct or revoke the decision or order. If the superior does not change the decision or order, or demands immediate execution, the civil servant shall execute the decision or order, and the superior shall bear the consequences of the execution, and the civil servant shall not bear liability. However, if the civil servant executes a decision or order that is manifestly illegal, the civil servant shall bear corresponding liability according to law.

Article 61 Where a civil servant shall bear disciplinary liability for violating discipline or law, an action shall be taken against him or her in accordance with this Law, or a governmental sanction shall be given by a supervisory organ according to law; if the violation is minor and the civil servant has corrected it after criticism and education, the action may be exempted.
Where a supervisory organ has already made a decision on governmental sanction for the same disciplinary or illegal act, the organ to which the civil servant belongs shall not take any action again.
Article 62 Actions are classified into: warning, demerit recording, serious demerit recording, demotion, removal from office, and dismissal.

Article 63 The action against a civil servant shall have clear facts, conclusive evidence, accurate characterization, proper handling, lawful procedures, and complete formalities.
Where a civil servant violates discipline or law, the organ that decides on the action shall decide to investigate the circumstances of the violation, and shall inform the civil servant of the facts ascertained through investigation and the basis for the proposed action. The civil servant shall have the right to make statements and defenses; the organ that decides on the action shall not aggravate the action because of the civil servant's defense.
Where the organ that decides on the action considers that an action shall be taken against a civil servant, it shall make a decision on the action within the prescribed time limit, in accordance with the administrative authority and the prescribed procedures. The decision on the action shall be notified to the civil servant in writing.

Article 64 A civil servant during the period of receiving an action shall not be promoted in post, rank or grade; in the case of receiving a demerit recording, serious demerit recording, demotion, or removal from office action, he or she shall not be promoted in the wage bracket.
The duration of action is: for warning, six months; for demerit recording, twelve months; for serious demerit recording, eighteen months; for demotion and removal from office, twenty-four months.
Where a civil servant receives a removal from office action, his or her grade shall be lowered according to the provisions.

Article 65 Where a civil servant who has received an action other than dismissal shows repentance during the period of action and does not commit any further disciplinary or illegal act, the action shall be automatically lifted upon expiration of the period.
After the lifting of the action, promotion of the wage bracket, grade, post, and rank shall no longer be affected by the original action. However, the lifting of a demotion or removal from office action shall not be deemed as restoration of the original grade, original post, or original rank.

Article 66 An organ shall, in accordance with the requirements of the civil servant's work duties and the need to improve the quality of civil servants, provide classified and graded training for civil servants.
The State shall establish specialized civil servant training institutions. An organ may also, as necessary, entrust other training institutions to undertake the task of civil servant training.

Article 67 An organ shall provide initial training for new recruits during the probation period; provide job-specific training for civil servants promoted to leadership posts before or within one year after assuming the post; provide specialized professional training for civil servants engaged in special work; and provide on-the-job training for all civil servants to improve political quality and work ability and update knowledge, among which technical training shall be provided for civil servants in professional and technical categories.
The State shall, in a planned manner, strengthen the training of outstanding young civil servants.

Article 68 Training for civil servants shall be subject to registration management.
The time for civil servants to participate in training shall be determined by the competent department of civil servants in accordance with the training requirements provided in Article 67 of this Law.
The training status and learning achievements of civil servants shall serve as one of the bases for evaluating civil servants and for appointment and promotion.

Article 69 The State shall practice a system of exchange for civil servants.
Civil servants may be exchanged within the ranks of civil servants and staff managed by reference to this Law, and may also be exchanged with persons engaged in public service in State-owned enterprises and public institutions not managed by reference to this Law.
The modes of exchange include transfer and reassignment.

Article 70 Persons engaged in public service in State-owned enterprises, institutions of higher education, scientific research institutes, and other public institutions not managed by reference to this Law may be transferred into an organ to assume leadership posts or ranks at the level of Fourth-Level Researcher or above and other equivalent ranks.
The candidate for transfer shall meet the conditions provided in Article 13 of this Law and the qualification requirements for the proposed post, and shall not have any circumstance provided in Article 26 of this Law. The transferring organ shall, in accordance with the above provisions, conduct a strict investigation of the candidate for transfer, and shall approve it according to the administrative authority; if necessary, an examination may be held for the candidate for transfer.

Article 71 The reassignment of a civil servant between different posts shall meet the qualification requirements for the proposed post, and shall be carried out within the prescribed staffing quotas and post numbers.
For leading members below the level of principal leadership at the provincial and ministerial level, cross-regional and cross-departmental reassignment shall be carried out in a planned and focused manner.
For civil servants holding leadership posts in internal organs and those with special work characteristics, reassignment within the organ shall be carried out in a planned manner.
Higher-level organs shall pay attention to openly selecting civil servants from grassroots organs.

Article 72 According to work needs, an organ may, by means of temporary assignment, select civil servants to undertake major projects, key tasks, or other special work.
During the period of temporary assignment, the personal relationship between the civil servant and the original organ shall not change.

Article 73 A civil servant shall comply with the exchange decision of the organ.
Where a civil servant applies for exchange on his or her own, it shall be approved according to the administrative authority.

Article 74 Civil servants who have a spousal relationship, lineal blood relationship, collateral blood relationship within three generations, or close in-law relationship shall not work in the same organ in posts where both are directly under the leadership of the same person or in posts with a direct superior-subordinate leadership relationship; nor shall they engage in organizational, personnel, disciplinary inspection, supervision, audit, or financial work in an organ where one of them holds a leadership post.
A civil servant shall not serve as a leading member in the industry regulatory or competent department of an enterprise or profit-making organization operated by his or her spouse, children, or children's spouses.
Where it is necessary to flexibly implement post avoidance due to special geographical or work characteristics, the competent department of civil servants at or above the provincial level shall provide regulations.

Article 75 Civil servants who assume principal leadership posts in township-level organs, county-level organs, and district-established municipal organs and their relevant departments shall implement territorial avoidance in accordance with relevant provisions.

Article 77 Where a civil servant falls under a circumstance requiring withdrawal, he or she shall apply for withdrawal; an interested party shall have the right to apply for the civil servant's withdrawal. Other persons may provide the organ with information about the civil servant's need for withdrawal.
The organ shall, based on the application of the civil servant or the interested party, make a decision on whether to withdraw after review, and may also directly make a withdrawal decision without an application.
Article 78 Where there are other provisions on civil servant withdrawal in laws, those provisions shall prevail.

Article 79 The civil servant system shall implement the salary system uniformly prescribed by the State.
The salary system for civil servants shall implement the principle of distribution according to work, reflecting factors such as work duties, work ability, work achievements, and seniority, and shall maintain a reasonable salary disparity among different leadership posts, ranks, and grades.
The State shall establish a normal salary increase mechanism for civil servants.

Article 80 The salary of civil servants shall include basic salary, allowances, subsidies, and bonuses.
Civil servants shall enjoy regional supplemental allowances, allowances for hardship and remote areas, post allowances, and other such allowances in accordance with State regulations.
Civil servants shall enjoy subsidies and allowances for housing, medical care, etc., in accordance with State regulations.
Civil servants who are evaluated as outstanding or competent in regular assessments shall enjoy year-end bonuses in accordance with State regulations.
Civil servants' salaries shall be paid in full and on time.

Article 81 The salary level of public servants shall be coordinated with the development of the national economy and be compatible with social progress.
The state shall implement a salary survey system, regularly conduct surveys and comparisons of the salary levels of public servants and comparable personnel in enterprises, and shall use the results of the salary survey and comparison as the basis for adjusting the salary level of public servants.

Article 82 Public servants shall enjoy welfare benefits in accordance with state regulations. The state shall raise the welfare benefits of public servants based on the level of economic and social development.
Public servants shall implement the working hours system prescribed by the state and enjoy vacations in accordance with state regulations. Where public servants work overtime beyond the statutory working days, they shall be granted corresponding compensatory leave; if compensatory leave cannot be granted, subsidies shall be provided in accordance with state regulations.

Article 83 Public servants shall participate in social insurance according to law and enjoy insurance benefits in accordance with state regulations.
Where a public servant dies in the line of duty or dies of illness, the public servant's relatives shall enjoy the pensions and preferential treatment prescribed by the state.

Article 84 No organ shall, in violation of state regulations, unilaterally modify the salary, welfare, and insurance policies for public servants, or arbitrarily increase or reduce the salary, welfare, and insurance benefits of public servants. No organ shall deduct or delay the payment of public servants' salaries.

Article 85 Where a public servant resigns from public office, the public servant shall submit a written application to the appointing and removing organ. The appointing and removing organ shall conduct examination and approval within thirty days from the date of receiving the application; for an application by a leading member to resign from public office, examination and approval shall be conducted within ninety days from the date of receiving the application.

Article 87 Where a public servant holding a leading position needs to resign from the current position due to a change in work in accordance with the provisions of law, the public servant shall go through the resignation formalities.
A public servant holding a leading position may voluntarily offer to resign from the leading position due to personal or other reasons.
Where a leading member causes significant losses or adverse social impact due to serious errors or dereliction of duty, or bears leadership responsibility for a major accident, the leading member shall assume responsibility and resign from the leading position.
Where a leading member is no longer suitable to hold the current leading position due to other reasons, or where the leading member should assume responsibility and resign but does not offer resignation, the leading member shall be ordered to resign from the leading position.

Article 90 The dismissal of a public servant shall be decided in accordance with the administrative authority. The dismissal decision shall be notified in writing to the dismissed public servant, and the basis and reasons for the dismissal shall be informed.
The dismissed public servant may receive a dismissal fee or enjoy unemployment insurance in accordance with the relevant provisions of the state.

Article 91 Where a public servant resigns or is dismissed, the public servant shall go through the formalities for the transfer of official business before leaving the post, and when necessary, shall accept an audit in accordance with regulations.
Article 92 Where a public servant has reached the retirement age prescribed by the state or has completely lost the ability to work, the public servant shall retire.

Article 94 After retirement, a public servant shall enjoy the pension and other benefits prescribed by the state. The state shall provide necessary services and assistance for the public servant's life and health, and encourage the public servant to give play to personal expertise and participate in social development.

Article 96 The original decision-making organ shall make a review decision within thirty days from the date of receiving the application for review and shall inform the applicant in writing. The organ that accepts the petition of a public servant shall make a decision on the matter within sixty days from the date of accepting the petition; if the case is complex, the time limit may be appropriately extended, but the extension shall not exceed thirty days.
The execution of the personnel decision shall not be suspended during the period of review or petition.
A public servant shall not be subjected to heavier handling due to applying for review or filing a petition.
Article 97 Where the organ accepting a public servant's petition finds through examination that the personnel decision is erroneous, the original decision-making organ shall promptly correct it.

Article 98 Where a public servant believes that an organ or its leading personnel infringes upon the public servant's lawful rights and interests, the public servant may, according to law, lodge a complaint with the organ at a higher level or with a supervisory organ. The organ that accepts the complaint shall handle it promptly in accordance with regulations.

Article 99 A public servant who files a petition or lodges a complaint shall respect the facts and shall not fabricate facts, make false accusations, or frame others. Where a public servant fabricates facts, makes false accusations, or frames others, the public servant shall be subject to legal liability according to law.

Article 100 Organs may, based on work needs and subject to approval by the public servant administration department at or above the provincial level, implement a contract appointment system for positions requiring strong specialized knowledge and auxiliary positions.
If the positions listed in the preceding paragraph involve state secrets, the contract appointment system shall not be implemented.

Article 101: A state organ may, when appointing civil servants by contract, conduct open recruitment by reference to the procedures for civil servant examination and recruitment, or directly select and appoint from among persons who meet the conditions.
The appointment of civil servants by contract by a state organ shall be carried out within the prescribed establishment quota and salary fund quota.

Article 102: When appointing civil servants by contract, a state organ shall, in accordance with the principles of equality, voluntariness, and reaching consensus through consultation, enter into a written appointment contract to specify the rights and obligations of both the state organ and the appointed civil servant. The appointment contract may be modified or rescinded upon consensus through consultation between the parties.
The conclusion, modification, or rescission of an appointment contract shall be reported to the civil servant competent authority at the same level for recordation.

Article 103: An appointment contract shall contain clauses on the term of the contract, the position and its duty requirements, remuneration, welfare, insurance benefits, and liability for breach of contract, among others.
The term of an appointment contract shall be from one to five years. A probation period may be stipulated in the appointment contract, which shall be from one to twelve months.
Civil servants appointed by contract shall implement a negotiated wage system, with specific measures to be prescribed by the central civil servant competent authority.
Article 104: A state organ shall manage the civil servants appointed by it in accordance with this Law and the appointment contract.

Article 105: Where a dispute arises between a civil servant appointed by contract and the appointing organ concerning the performance of the appointment contract, an application for arbitration may be filed within sixty days from the date the dispute arises.
The civil servant competent authorities at or above the provincial level shall establish a personnel dispute arbitration commission as needed to accept arbitration applications. The personnel dispute arbitration commission shall be composed of representatives from the civil servant competent authority, representatives of the appointing organ, representatives of the civil servants appointed by contract, and legal experts.
Where a party disagrees with the arbitration award, it may initiate a prosecution with the People's Court within fifteen days from the date of receiving the written arbitration award. After the arbitration award takes effect, if one party fails to perform it, the other party may apply to the People's Court for enforcement.

Article 107: Where a civil servant resigns from public office or retires, if the civil servant was originally a leading member or held a leading position at or above the county and division level, within three years after leaving office, and other civil servants within two years after leaving office, they shall not hold a position in an enterprise or other for-profit organization directly related to their original duties, nor shall they engage in profit-making activities directly related to their original duties.
Where a civil servant who has resigned or retired violates the provisions of the preceding paragraph, the civil servant competent authority at the same level as the original appointing organ shall order correction within a specified time limit; if correction is not made within the time limit, the market regulation authority at or above the county level shall confiscate the illegal income gained by such person during the period of employment, order the receiving entity to dismiss such person, and, depending on the seriousness of the circumstances, impose on the receiving entity a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal income of the punished person.

Article 108: Where any staff member of the civil servant competent authority, in violation of the provisions of this Law, abuses power, neglects duties, or engages in irregularities for personal gain, if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if a crime is not constituted, a sanction shall be imposed, or a disciplinary sanction shall be imposed by the supervisory authority according to law.

Article 109: Where, in the course of civil servant recruitment, appointment by contract, or other work, there are acts such as concealing truthful information, engaging in fraud, cheating in examinations, or disrupting the order of examinations, the civil servant competent authority shall, depending on the circumstances, render a disposition such as invalidating examination results, disqualifying the person, or restricting the person from taking examinations; where the circumstances are serious, legal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 110: Where a state organ, due to an erroneous personnel action, causes damage to the reputation of a civil servant, it shall make an apology, restore the reputation, and eliminate the adverse effects; where economic losses are caused, compensation shall be given according to law.
Article 111: For the purposes of this Law, "leading members" refers to the leading personnel of a state organ, excluding those who hold leading positions in the internal organs of the state organ.

Article 112: Staff members, other than service workers, of public institutions authorized by laws and regulations to exercise public affairs management functions may, upon approval, be managed by reference to this Law.
Article 113: This Law shall come into force as of June 1, 2019.
